en.title: Warehouse Connection Cost With Added Hubs
en.description:
Warehouse capacities are in non-decreasing order. Warehouse i connects to the nearest hub j with j not less than i, at cost capacity[j]−capacity[i]. Warehouse n is always a hub. Each query independently adds two hubs, hubA and hubB; output the total connection cost. The source example's 13 is wrong; by the definition, the correct cost is 5.

Standard input/output, examples and judging were written independently by CSWork; conventions marked as this site's do not claim to be the source's original limits.
en.input: The first line contains n q (3≤n≤200000, 1≤q≤200000); the second line contains n non-decreasing capacities (1..10⁹); each of the next q lines contains A B, with 1≤A<B<n.
en.output: Output q integers in query order.
en.explanation: Example 1: the hubs are 1, 3 and 5; the warehouse costs are 0, 2, 0, 3, 0, for a total of 5. Example 2: all capacities are equal, so the cost is 0. Example 3: with hubs 1, 2 and 4, only warehouse 3 pays 10−6=4; with hubs 2, 3 and 4, only warehouse 1 pays 3−1=2.
hints: Use prefix sums to compute the three segments that connect to A, B and n separately; each segment costs segment length × hub capacity − the sum of capacities in the segment.
